name: alaska-otters
description: Morphometric measurements and reproductive and dependency status for sea otters captured or collected in Alaska by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), 1947-2019.

tables.name: otters
tables.description: One row per otter. Of the 4,507 otters, 113 have measurements from more than one capture or collection event.

columns.name: otter_no
columns.description: Identifier assigned by researchers. Naming conventions vary by location and period, but identifiers are not reused. Two unnamed measured pups were assigned synthetic-1 and synthetic-2 during cleaning.

columns.name: sex
columns.description: Sex recorded for the otter.

columns.name: recap
columns.description: Whether the otter was recorded as recaptured. This agrees with the number of measurements rows except for SW-155, which is marked as recaptured but has one row, and SO-04-05a, which is marked as captured once but has two. The latter's 2008-05-18 row may belong to pup SO-04-05b.

tables.name: measurements
tables.description: One row per capture or collection event. An otter caught more than once has multiple rows. This includes 173 dependent-pup measurements separated from fields on the accompanying female's record during cleaning.

columns.name: measurement_id
columns.description: Identifier assigned during cleaning to each capture or collection event. Values run from 1 to 4,643 and have no source-data meaning.

columns.name: otter_no
columns.description: Identifier of the otter captured or collected.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Date of capture or collection. Together with otter_no, this identifies an event except for KWK-59-162: a post-captivity weighing appears to retain the original capture date rather than the weighing date of 1959-05-13.

columns.name: location
columns.description: Local place name for the capture or collection site. See locations for its region and area.

columns.name: lat
columns.description: Latitude of capture or collection location in decimal degrees (WGS84).

columns.name: long
columns.description: Longitude of capture or collection location in decimal degrees (WGS84).

columns.name: weight
columns.description: Otter weight in kilograms.

columns.name: tail_lgth
columns.description: Mean tail length in centimeters. Individual measurements are in replicates.

columns.name: curvilinear
columns.description: Whether length was measured along the curve of the back rather than in a straight line. The source recorded this as the 0.974 conversion factor, which is already applied in true_standard_lgth. It is unknown for the 173 dependent-pup events separated from their mother's record during cleaning.

columns.name: lgth
columns.description: Mean standard length including the tail, in centimeters. Individual measurements are in replicates; four events have a value only here.

columns.name: true_standard_lgth
columns.description: Length including the tail, standardized across measurement protocols, in centimeters. It equals lgth for standard measurements and curve_lgth multiplied by 0.974 for curvilinear measurements.

columns.name: body_lgth
columns.description: Body length excluding the tail, in centimeters, calculated as true_standard_lgth - tail_lgth. Available for the 401 events where both values are known.

columns.name: curve_lgth
columns.description: Curvilinear length including the tail, in centimeters. It was measured once per event and therefore has no rows in replicates.

columns.name: curve_lgth_alt
columns.description: Unidentified length in centimeters, named CURVE_LGTH2 in the source but not a replicate of curve_lgth. Its 21 values are from 2006-03-29 to 2006-04-08 at nknight and montague and exceed curve_lgth by 12-23 cm. What was measured is unknown.

columns.name: girth
columns.description: Mean chest circumference at the xiphoid, in centimeters. Individual measurements are in replicates.

columns.name: paw
columns.description: Maximum front-paw width in millimeters.

columns.name: w_pup
columns.description: Dependency status at capture or collection. Y without a pup_number means a pup was seen but not identified; 251 events have this combination, and those pups have no rows of their own.

value_labels.D: The individual is the dependent pup

columns.name: pup_number
columns.description: Identifier of the dependent pup accompanying the female. Measurements stored on the female's source record were separated into an event for the pup during cleaning.

columns.name: fetus_pres
columns.description: Fetal presence at collection. The code matches the number of related fetuses rows: none for N, one for Y, and two or three for M.

columns.name: fe_rep_con
columns.description: Reproductive condition recorded for a female.

columns.name: fe_rep_sta
columns.description: Parity recorded for a collected female.

columns.name: pregnancy_status
columns.description: Pregnancy status at capture or collection.

value_labels.NP: Not pregnant at collection or capture
value_labels.P: Fetus present at collection or palpably pregnant at capture
value_labels.PP: Not documented in the source metadata

columns.name: can_dia
columns.description: Maximum canine-tooth diameter at the gum line, in millimeters.

columns.name: final_age
columns.description: Age at capture or collection, in years, based on known age, tooth cementum, or a field estimate.

columns.name: age_category
columns.description: Broad age class at capture or collection.

columns.name: bacula_lgth
columns.description: Baculum length in centimeters, recorded for males.

columns.name: comments
columns.description: Free-text notes about the otter or event.
examples: pup < 8 wks later but preg missed at capture

columns.name: cause_of_death_capture_method
columns.description: Capture or collection method.

value_labels.captivity: Measured after some time in captivity

tables.name: replicates
tables.description: One row per individual tail-length, standard-length, or girth measurement. Tail length has multiple measurements for 287 of 403 events, standard length for 160 of 2,269, and girth for 4 of 1,052. Replicated tail lengths differ by a median of 0.5 cm.

columns.name: measurement_id
columns.description: Identifier of the capture or collection event.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Measurement type. The corresponding measurements column contains the mean for the event.

value_labels.girth: Circumference of chest at xiphoid, 29.5 to 96.5 cm
value_labels.lgth: Length of otter including tail, 40.2 to 148.2 cm

columns.name: replicate
columns.description: Sequence number in source order, starting at 1. Girth has at most two measurements per event.

columns.name: value
columns.description: Measurement in centimeters, recorded to one decimal place. See quantity for type-specific ranges.

tables.name: locations
tables.description: One row per named capture or collection place, with its region and area.

columns.name: location
columns.description: Place name recorded for capture or collection events.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Alaska region containing the place; a region may contain multiple areas.

columns.name: area
columns.description: Alaska area containing the place.

tables.name: fetuses
tables.description: One row per fetus found in a collected female. A collection with multiple fetuses has multiple rows.

columns.name: measurement_id
columns.description: Identifier of the collection event at which the fetus was found.

columns.name: fetus_num
columns.description: Index distinguishing fetuses within a collection, numbered from 1 in no meaningful order; it is not a fetus count.

columns.name: fetus_sex
columns.description: Sex recorded for the fetus.

columns.name: fetus_wt
columns.description: Fetal weight in grams.

columns.name: fetus_lth
columns.description: Fetal length in centimeters.

relationships.description: Links each otter to its capture or collection events.
Links an event to its individual tail-length, standard-length, and girth measurements. The 2,370 events with none of these measurements have no related rows.
Links a collection event to fetuses found in the female.
Links an event to the region and area containing its location.

Links an event involving a female with a named dependent pup to that pup. Each of the 388 named pups has an otters row; when pup measurements are available, they appear in the pup's own same-day measurements row.

glossary.definition: Length measured along the curve of the back while the otter lies on its stomach, used primarily during experimental harvests from 1967 to 1971.
Straight-line length measured while the otter lies on its back, used from 1947 to 1963 and from 1986 to 2019.
Length standardized across protocols: standard length is unchanged, while curvilinear length is multiplied by 0.974.
Controlled collection of sea otters for research, primarily during the 1960s and 1970s.
A female that has never given birth.
A female that has given birth once.
A female that has given birth multiple times.
Penile bone, whose length can be used to estimate age class.
Lower portion of the sternum, used as the landmark for girth measurements.
